body:
Two controls that are each correct in isolation combine into a deadlock: **a PR whose base branch
moves cannot be brought up to date, and therefore cannot merge.**

1. The `main` ruleset sets `required_status_checks` with
   `strict_required_status_checks_policy: true`, so a branch reporting `BEHIND` is refused.
2. `~/.config/git/hooks/pre-push` (identity firewall) requires every OUTGOING commit's author and
   committer to be `new-usemame <248195428+…>`. Commits on `main` are GitHub squash-merges whose
   committer is `GitHub <noreply@github.com>`.

So merging `origin/main` into a topic branch produces a fast-forward push whose range includes
main's commits, and the hook refuses it:

    PUSH BLOCKED by identity firewall
    Outgoing commits that do not match:
    d4075037e1 CWNG Maintainer nate <…> / GitHub <noreply@github.com>
    …

OBSERVED 2026-08-29 on `fix/locale-validated-on-write` (PR #1978), which went `BEHIND` by 5 commits
while its CI ran.

The hook already contains the correct logic — it just does not reach it. It picks its range thus:

    non-fast-forward (a rebased branch):  $local_sha --not --remotes
    fast-forward:                         $remote_sha..$local_sha

`--not --remotes` excludes anything already on a remote-tracking ref, so main's commits are
correctly ignored for a rebased branch. That path was added 2026-08-28 and is operator-approved. A
forward-MERGE is equally legitimate and the same exclusion is equally correct for it, but it takes
the other branch and gets swept.

The result is that the only way to update a `BEHIND` branch is to rebase and force-push — which the
autopilot's own working rules discourage for a branch that already has an open PR, because it
breaks review links. Between the two, a session with a moving base has no compliant path forward.
This is a strong candidate for the mechanism behind F-c95945 ("tier-1 auto-merge stalls forever
once a PR goes BEHIND").

FIX SHAPE: use `$local_sha --not --remotes` unconditionally. It is strictly more precise than the
range form in both cases — it asks exactly the intended question, "which commits am I introducing
that the remote does not already have?" — and it does not weaken the firewall, because any commit
genuinely new to the remote is still checked on both author and committer.

NOT worked around here. Bypassing an identity firewall with `--no-verify` is explicitly forbidden,
and editing the operator's security hook to unblock my own PR is not a change I should make
unilaterally. PR #1978 is left `BEHIND` and unmergeable, with its branch reset to the pushed state
so nothing is half-applied.
title: The identity firewall blocks forward-merging main, so a PR whose base moves can never satisfy the strict up-to-date rule
